data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol elevates a crash-without-terminal-record to a Byzantine fault scenario, requiring a Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus among independent storage witnesses that the workspace contains no completed evidence before reclamation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The storage nodes may not be independent and may suffer correlated failures, violating BFT assumptions.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The workspace may be private or encrypted, preventing witnesses from inspecting contents to issue emptiness proofs without violating confidentiality.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"BFT overhead may render reclamation impractical for systems with high workspace churn or tight latency requirements.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Because the crashed process cannot testify to its own workspace contents, the protocol treats all such workspaces as potentially adversarial. Reclamation proceeds only after BFT consensus among a quorum of storage nodes confirms that no evidence-carrying object exists in the workspace region. The durably recorded artifact is the BFT-signed emptiness certificate, not the workspace contents. This guarantees that silent displacement cannot occur unless a supermajority of witnesses is compromised.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
